hero.name: Neil Chen
hero.headline: Turning QA experience into systems that AI follows.
hero.lead: Software Test Automation Engineer at QNAP with five years of testing storage systems (ZFS, high availability, snapshots). My focus now is taking the whole test workflow — spec review, case design, on-device execution, bug filing and verification, reporting — and building it into a system that AI agents run unattended, with a review gate at every step.

about.label: About
about.title: What I do now
about.intro: I work where QA meets AI engineering: I know what it takes for a test to count, and I can write that judgement as rules an AI can read, follow, and be stopped by when it gets them wrong.

pillars.title: AI agent work systems
pillars.body: I keep my way of working in a version-controlled "brain" repository: Skills define how to do things, a knowledge base records facts and past mistakes, and review agents check work before anything is written. Any machine that clones it has the same abilities.

pillars.title: Test engineering
pillars.body: Finding logic gaps in specs, designing scenarios, writing automation, running it on real devices and judging the result. Evidence comes first: every conclusion traces back to raw output, and every verification has a control run that proves the measurement can detect the problem.
points: Spec review and test case design
Bug reproduction, root cause, fix verification

pillars.title: Storage domain knowledge
pillars.body: Long-term owner of core storage features on a ZFS-based NAS operating system: high-availability clusters, storage pools and RAID, snapshots and backup. That knowledge decides whether AI output is usable — you can only catch an AI's mistake if you know which result makes no sense.

ai.label: AI Work
ai.title: AI in production use
ai.intro: This is not about having AI write a few snippets. It is about handing the whole workflow to AI and designing enough gates that the result can be trusted. These systems run in my daily work today.

featured.title: Multi-machine AI fleet: an unattended test team
featured.summary: Six virtual machines became AI nodes that share one "brain". A supervisor plans and dispatches, five workers take tasks. I leave one line in a chat app, or a ticket gets assigned, and the fleet starts working, then reports the result and the lesson it learned.
bullets: The supervisor splits work by task type, dispatches, tracks, and pauses new tasks when usage reaches a threshold
Risk tiers: read-only and low-risk actions run on their own; creating tickets, pushing code and changing settings need my approval
Three gates on every push: nodes cannot push by default, and need a passed review plus a one-time code
Every task report carries a lesson, which a retrospective step files into the knowledge base

featured.title: The full test workflow on AI: from spec to report
featured.summary: A spec ticket comes in and AI works through spec review, test planning, naming, UI exploration, writing steps and uploading to the case management system. In the test phase it writes the scripts, runs them on real devices, judges each failure, files bugs and writes the report. Each stage is a Skill, and independent review agents sit between stages.
bullets: Spec review produces a confirmation list for the PM: background, an options table and a recommendation per item
Test plans get a second review across seven aspects: coverage matrix, redundancy, gaps, fidelity to the spec and more
Case data has a single source; fixes and uploads both start from the same file
Each failure is judged against the latest spec: real failure, spec changed, or misjudgement — each with its own follow-up

featured.title: Review before write: making AI output trustworthy
featured.summary: Anything irreversible or costly — filing a bug, uploading test cases, pushing code — first goes to a fresh agent that took no part in writing it. The reviewer re-reads the rules, returns only pass or fail, does not fix the work, and does not accept the author's conclusion.
bullets: 7 review agents: bug drafts, test plans, case uploads, automation scripts, code, push safety
Code review targets failures reported as success, edge cases and platform differences
Before a push: scan for secrets and files that should not be committed, and check the scope of authorisation
At most three rounds per piece of work; a deadlock goes to a human

featured.title: A version-controlled knowledge base: long-term memory for AI
featured.summary: An AI starts every conversation from zero, so what is worth keeping goes into the repository: platform facts, diagnostic criteria, case context, methods, and a "misjudgement library" of traps that look like A but are B. The lookup order is fixed — method, then fact, then misjudgement — and commands are looked up before they are run, not tried out on a device.
bullets: 13 platform and version fact sheets, 27 case files, 13 method documents
19 misjudgement traps: one entry for every misleading symptom solved
Rejected options have a decision log, read before anyone proposes them again
Every session ends with a retrospective: what becomes a Skill, an agent, or a knowledge-base entry

featured.title: Customer issue reproduction and root cause analysis
featured.summary: The path from a customer report to a reproduction on a real device, written as a method: collect context, parse the diagnostic bundle, design a plan that tells hypotheses apart, build and measure, then reverse the change to confirm. A dedicated agent parses the bundle and returns only the conclusion.
bullets: Discriminating experiments: each one must rule out a hypothesis
Performance issues are first split into busy versus abnormal, and need dataset, disk and memory data before any conclusion
Memory leak verification: baseline, load, four checkpoints and a long sampling curve
Developers receive a replay guide they can run themselves, not just a conclusion

featured.title: UI testing and bug fix verification
featured.summary: The action under test always goes through the web UI; the command line only creates data, reads back and cleans up. UI fixes are not checked by eye: each item is asserted with DOM geometry, and a control run with the fix disabled proves the measurement really detects the bug.
bullets: End-to-end snapshot tests across three operating system generations
Localisation checks: all languages compared at file level, plus screenshots from the real UI
Each case builds its own environment and tears it down, never relying on existing resources
Automatic screenshots and phase-by-phase reports, traceable for pass and fail alike

items.title: Report generator
items.desc: Reproduction, verification, test and performance reports share one skeleton and visual template, output as a single HTML file; every number traces back to raw data.

items.title: Token usage control
items.desc: Measurement showed over 40k tokens resent on every call. The main instruction file went from 68KB to 17KB, with rule text moved out and read only when needed.

items.title: Ticket system automation
items.desc: Queries, labels, comments, status, assignment, due dates, tickets and sub-tasks are all driven by natural language, with a hook adding the tracking label afterwards.

items.title: Enterprise platform integration
items.desc: Lets AI read document libraries, wiki pages, team channel messages and meeting recording transcripts, handling authentication on its own.

items.title: Weekly report automation
items.desc: Scans the week's AI sessions and code commits, compiles an AI usage report and a Git activity record, and creates and updates the record tickets.

items.title: NAS test toolkit
items.desc: Batch snapshots, CPU monitoring, build alignment checks, debug log switches and environment health checks — each one a Skill.

items.title: AI-assisted Robot Framework development
items.desc: AI analyses the existing framework and conventions, then produces compliant cases and refactors old scripts in bulk; 27+ cases and 25+ shared keywords so far.

items.title: CI stress test monitoring
items.desc: Checks several stress test jobs and device builds in one go, and analyses the cause when one fails.
